newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico denies drug lord arrest warrant overturned.
newsitem.headline: Mexico denies drug lord arrest warrant overturned.

text.p: Mexican authorities, under pressure from Washington to demonstrate commitment in the war on drugs, on Wednesday denied news reports that an arrest warrant against the country's most powerful drug baron had been overturned by a judge.
"It is reiterated that the arrest warrant against Amado Carrillo Fuentes is still legally solid," the Attorney General's Office said in a statement.
It said some news media had carried items saying Carrillo, known as the "Lord of the Skies" and the head of the powerful Juarez drugs cartel, had received an "amparo," protecting him from arrest.
An "amparo" is a ruling in Mexican law, similar to "habeas corpus" in Anglo-Saxon law, protecting the beneficiary from illegal imprisonment.
The Attorney General's Office said a judge had overturned in March last year one "amparo" obtained by Carrillo and that another judge had recently rejected another application.

President Bill Clinton must decide in the coming days whether to "certify" that Mexico is cooperating with Washington in its war on drugs. Countries that fail the annual U.S. review may face U.S sanctions.
